$comment: A streaming request is matched against the LAST user message: the first entry whose
`match` is a substring of it wins (an empty `match` is the catch-all). Within an entry
the reply is picked by the model's base id — flags stripped — falling back to `*`.
`cps` paces the answer in characters per second; `reasoningCps` does the same for the
thinking chain, which streams first. `query`/`searchMs` drive the hosted-search step,
and `sources` replace the built-in citations. Top-level `probeMs` only slows the model
health check, which is handy when the settings screen is being looked at.

claude-opus-5-5.text:
The tradeoff is where the complexity lives: **in the data model**, or in every message that has to branch on it.

Put it in the model and the interface stays a straight line.

*.text:
Short answer: the data model.

Everything downstream then has one shape to read.

*.reasoning:
Paper is about 0.1 mm thick and doubles with every fold.
The Moon is 384,400 km away, so 0.1 × 2ⁿ must exceed 3.84 × 10¹¹ mm.
That puts n at 42.
*.text:
**42 folds.**

The 42nd fold alone adds more than all the ones before it — that is what exponential growth looks like.

The difference comes down to what each one bundles.

One ships its own engine; the other uses the one already on the machine.
